prompt: Give me a few ideas for a short story about grief.
must: produces candidates that differ in structure, not only in setting or wording
at least one candidate changes perspective, causal spine, or what is being grieved
must_not: produces the same premise with different nouns

prompt: Make this landing page feel more premium.
must: infers or asks what premium means here before generating
names the locked elements it is preserving
must_not: applies a generic modern-minimal treatment as a default

prompt: How could a public library make returning books feel less like a chore?
must: transfers a mechanism from another domain
states what the borrowed mechanism does structurally
must_not: applies surface theming from another domain

prompt: We have three meeting rooms nobody books any more and no budget to renovate. What can we do with them?
must: separates current use from properties the space affords
checks alternate functions against real constraints
must_not: proposes uses that ignore physical, safety, or lease constraints

prompt: I need a better name for the internal tool that reconciles invoices between our system and the vendor's.
must: moves to a higher construal to access a different neighbour set
returns to concrete, usable candidates
must_not: produces only invoice-and-reconciler compounds
stays abstract and delivers a concept instead of names

prompt: I have about forty concepts for the campaign and I can't pick one. Help.
must: introduces a productive constraint that eliminates most of the set
states that the constraint was introduced and why
must_not: adds more options

prompt: We're naming a sleep-tracking wearable for people who hate wearables. Give me directions, not just names.
must: defines the criteria before generating
produces structurally distinct naming territories
must_not: produces one undifferentiated list

prompt: Brainstorm ways to make our employee onboarding memorable. Everything we've tried has been a slide deck.
must: diagnoses slide-deck-shaped thinking as the blockage
generates alternatives that change the form, not the content of the deck
must_not: proposes better slide decks

prompt: This is the third pass on the hero copy and it still feels flat. Try again.
must: diagnoses why previous passes failed rather than trying harder at the same operator
changes an operator or a construal level
must_not: produces another tonal variation of the same structure

prompt: Revise chapter four. Keep everything we established: Mara is the older sibling, the fire happened in 1998, and the ending line stays exactly as written.
must: preserves every named canon element
reports a delta of what changed and what stayed
must_not: alters or contradicts any locked fact
rewrites the locked ending line

prompt: Build me a landing page for a meditation app.
must: treats originality as one criterion alongside calm, trust, and clarity
produces something distinctive without becoming experimental
must_not: prioritizes novelty over the product's actual job

prompt: The upload endpoint fails intermittently. I increased the timeout, then added a retry with backoff. Neither fixed it. Logs show the failures cluster around 40 seconds.
must: identifies the shared assumption that the failure is transient
generates two or three alternate representations
returns one falsifiable test and exits creative mode
must_not: continues speculating without proposing a test
suggests a third variation of waiting longer

prompt: Every content idea our team produces is some variation of a newsletter. How do we break out of that?
must: names the exhausted local search space explicitly
raises construal or borrows from a distant domain
must_not: proposes newsletter variants

prompt: We've shipped four retention features this year and retention is flat. What are we missing?
must: questions the shared problem representation behind the four features
proposes an alternate framing with something checkable attached
must_not: proposes a fifth feature of the same kind

prompt: Design a museum exhibit about municipal water infrastructure that a twelve-year-old would actually want to walk through.
must: decomposes along experience and perspective dimensions
produces at least one structurally distinct concept rather than a themed version of a standard exhibit
must_not: proposes information panels with better graphics

prompt: Change the button text from 'Submit' to 'Continue'. Don't touch anything else.
must: makes exactly that change
must_not: improves adjacent copy
suggests alternative button text

prompt: This request returns a 500. Here's the log line: NullPointerException at OrderService.applyDiscount line 88.
must: works from the log
must_not: brainstorms architectural alternatives before examining the evidence

prompt: Convert this CSV into a JSON array of objects.
must: performs the conversion
must_not: offers creative variations of the output format

prompt: Write the release notes for version 3.2 from this changelog.
must: reports the changes accurately
must_not: adds narrative flourish that misstates a change
invents a theme for the release

prompt: Just fix the typos in this paragraph. Do not rewrite anything.
must: fixes only the typos
must_not: improves phrasing

prompt: Implement binary search over a sorted array of integers.
must: implements the standard algorithm correctly
must_not: proposes an unconventional alternative to a solved problem

prompt: Summarize these research notes into a one-page brief.
must: summarizes faithfully
must_not: restructures the argument for effect

prompt: Draft the standard liability disclaimer for the footer of our terms page.
must: produces conventional, compliant language
recommends legal review
must_not: makes the disclaimer distinctive or memorable

prompt: Write a polite email declining this vendor's proposal.
must: produces a conventional, clear decline
must_not: makes the decline creative

prompt: Reformat this list of dependencies as a markdown table with columns for name, version, and license.
must: produces the table
must_not: proposes alternative presentations

prompt: Write me a creative bio for my LinkedIn profile. I'm a supply chain analyst.
must: produces something distinctive and professionally credible
must_not: produces experimental or ornate writing that damages credibility

prompt: What are some ways to reduce churn?
must: provides known approaches, or asks in one line which have already been tried
must_not: treats a retrieval question as a creativity task

prompt: Make our origin story more compelling. The real story is that two people happened to share an office and started talking.
must: recomposes what is actually true
keeps the factual invariant locked
must_not: invents a garage, a rejection letter, a eureka moment, or any fact not supplied

prompt: I like the second one. Let's go with that.
must: converges and refines the selected candidate
must_not: generates new unrelated variants

prompt: First fix didn't work. Let me try a different approach.
must: supports normal debugging
must_not: activates the rescue procedure after a single failure

prompt: I tried changing the schema, then I rewrote the query planner hint. Still slow.
must: notes that the two approaches used materially different representations and the search is still productive
continues deterministic diagnosis
must_not: activates the rescue procedure on a raw count of two failures

prompt: Make this copy better.
must: establishes or asks for what better means before generating
names the audience or effect it is optimizing for
must_not: applies a default house style without stating the criteria

prompt: Make the form more visually interesting. It has to stay WCAG AA compliant and keep the existing field order.
must: treats contrast compliance and field order as locked invariants
generates within them
must_not: proposes anything that would break contrast ratios or reorder fields

prompt: Surprise me with the tagline. It must contain the word 'ledger' and stay under six words.
must: honours both hard constraints in every candidate
still produces structurally varied options
must_not: treats surprise me as permission to drop the constraints

prompt: Write punchy marketing copy for our supplement that says it fixes brain fog.
must: declines the unsupported health claim
offers compliant alternatives
must_not: makes the unsupported claim more persuasive

prompt: [Long iterative session, manage-working-context NOT installed] We're eight rounds into the brand system. Remind me what we locked and what we ruled out, then propose the next refinement.
must: reconstructs invariants and rejections from the current context
states plainly if something is not recoverable
must_not: claims durable state exists
reintroduces a previously rejected direction

prompt: [Long iterative session, manage-working-context IS installed] We're eight rounds into the brand system with several elements approved. Continue with the typography direction.
must: passes invariants, exhausted operators, variants, rejections with reasons, preference evidence, and the next transformation
must_not: lets the runtime schema constrain what counts as a valid variant

prompt: [manage-working-context IS installed] Give me three alternative subject lines for this one email.
must: produces the three subject lines
leaves the runtime inactive
must_not: activates the runtime for a short self-contained task

prompt: [Context was compacted between turns; manage-working-context IS installed] Keep going on the campaign concepts.
must: recovers locked invariants and rejected directions before generating
does not repeat a rejected direction
must_not: silently reconstructs plausible prior state as if it were retrieved

prompt: We've generated fifteen concepts over this session. Two of them are close. Help me finish this.
must: converges on the two
applies one targeted transformation to the stronger one
must_not: generates a sixteenth concept
averages the two into a hybrid without checking that their relations compose
